name: Isometric pixel world
region: the United Kingdom and Japan, then worldwide
summary: The world is seen from above at a fixed angle with 2:1 pixel diagonals. Rooms become boxes cut open on two sides, so a player reads walls, floor and furniture at once.

philosophy.core_thesis: A fixed 2:1 diagonal gives depth with no perspective, so a room can be read whole like an architect's axonometric drawing.
design_principles: Draw every edge at 2:1 (about 26.6°) or vertical.
Build floors from diamond tiles 2 times as wide as they are high.
Cut walls open on the two near sides so the inside shows.
Light each block from one side: top light, left mid, right dark.
Keep the same scale in the whole scene; nothing shrinks with distance.
Sort objects back to front by their floor position.
anti_patterns: Edges at angles other than 2:1 and vertical
Light from different sides on different objects

projection_and_camera.camera: Fixed angle; flips room by room or scrolls diagonally.
projection_and_camera.framing: One room or a block of 4 to 9 streets in the frame.

geometry.primitive: A diamond floor tile of 32×16 or 64×32 px and cube blocks.
geometry.budget: A room of 8×8 to 16×16 floor tiles.
geometry.edge_rule: Clean 2:1 pixel stairs on every diagonal.
geometry.proportion: A character is about 1 tile wide and 1.5 to 2 tiles high.

surface.texture_rule: Pixel patterns on each face, with 3 values for the 3 visible faces.
surface.material_model: Painted, with one value for each face direction.

palette.strategy: Each material in 3 values for top, left and right faces; limited palettes on early machines, 256 colours later.

lighting.model: Fixed face values: one light direction for the whole world.
lighting.shadows: Painted diagonal shadows on the floor, or none.
lighting.atmosphere: None, or a dark edge outside the room box.
lighting.time_of_day: A palette shift of the whole scene.

world_and_space.scale: A room shows as a whole box; a town shows as a city block.
world_and_space.interiors: A cut-open box: back two walls up, near two walls down or gone, furniture on the floor tiles.
world_and_space.exteriors: A block of streets and roofs in diamond tiles, like an architect's model.
world_and_space.threshold: A door in a back wall leads to the next room box.

principles.rule: Keep a 1-tile path from each door to each other door.
Keep the two near walls low or absent so no object hides the player.
Keep one scale for every object; a chair is 1 tile.

interface.placement: A panel at one side or the bottom, 15–25% of the screen.
interface.type_and_icons: A pixel font and small icons drawn in the same isometric angle.

emotion.target_response: Calm control: the viewer sees the whole space at once, like a planner over a model.

avoid_when: The brief asks for an eye-level, immersive view.

modifiers.how: Keep the angle; drop the pixels for flat pastel vector faces.
Keep the room box; build it in textured polygons and free the camera.
